text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
STANDART
-- Bulgaria sold 60 percent of its Sodi Devnya chemical company to the U.S. firm General Chemical Group for $160 million, deputy prime minister Rumen Gechev said.
The buyer also pledged to invest $118 million in Sodi over the next five years.
-- The cabinet lowered the limit for duty free imports for Bulgarians to $100 from $300 worth, effective from today. @

-- The governing Socialist party's Supreme Council will call an urgent plenum on Tuesday to finalise details of the agenda for a party congress expected to be held on December 21-22, the newspaper said without qouting sources.
-- Bulgarian customs officers seized four kilogrammes of heroin on Wednesday from two Macedonians trying to enter Bulgaria from Turkey by car, customs officals said.
TRUD
-- Bulgaria's cabinet hiked electricity and coal prices by 9.7 percent and fuel prices by 14-18 percent in line with inflation and the lev/dollar exchange rate, effective from today.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet decided to grant concession rights on its Black Sea beaches to private operators for a period of three to five years, a government official said.
-- Bulgaria's Energy Minister Roumen Ovcharov is expected to visit Turkey on Monday to discuss possible exports of Bulgarian electricity and the transit of Russian natural gas through Bulgaria.
-- Five-star hotels in Bulgaria's capital Sofia rank second after Moscow's in a list of the most expensive hotels in the world, a DHL courier service company survey showed.
-- The Russian private companies Elit and Rif and the Swiss Union Financial International were interested in buying Bulgaria's forklift truck producer Balkankar holding.
Bulgaria expects to receive some 15 billion levs from the sale, deputy industry minister Valentin Grozdanov said.
PARI
-- Bulgaria's central bank (BNB) cancelled the licences of another four finacial houses for violating BNB's trading regulations. The BNB canceled the licences of 22 financial houses on October 31.

-- There will be no gas pipeline for a transit of Russian natural gas through Bulgaria to its Balkan neighbours if the Bulgarian government persists on concession conditions that are considered unfavourable by Moscow, the outgoing Russian ambassador to Sofia Alexander Avdeyev said.
24 CHASA

-- Nine Bulgarian state and private banks mailed abroad 2.811 tonnes of foreign currency notes registered as valuable dispatches through the Sofia airport in the first six months of 1996, a parlamentarian said in a report on uncontrolled siphoning of funds out of Bulgaria.
One million dollars in $100 bills weighs 8 killogrammes, a the parliamentarian said.
-- The international audit of Bulgaria's central bank (BNB) by the auditing company Deloitte & Touche was completed on Thursday, a BNB official said.
NOVINAR

-- The Bulgarian lev might slump to 350 per dollar at the end of the year to facilitate the introduction of a currency board system proposed by the International Monetary Fund to stabilise the country's economy, the newspaper said quoting unidentified experts.

Under the currency board system, which pegs the local currency to a major currency, the amount of levs in circulation must be exactly matched by the country's foreign exhcahge reserves. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
